# PlotSpectra – quick start

*Generated by Ali Bazrafkan | ali.bazrafkan@montana.edu*

## Install (once, ~5 minutes)

1. Install Python 3.10 or newer from https://www.python.org/downloads/ — on Windows tick **"Add python.exe to PATH"**.
2. Unzip `PlotSpectra_v*.zip` anywhere (for example `Documents\PlotSpectra`).
3. Double-click **`PlotSpectra.bat`** (Windows) or **`PlotSpectra.command`** (macOS/Linux).
   The first start creates a private environment and downloads the packages; later starts take seconds.

That is all. The app opens in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:8765. Keep the black window open while you work.

## Use (3 inputs, 1 click)

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 · Data | Pick the Pix4Dfields export folder (the one with `Orthomosaic.data.tif` and `Surface model.data.tif`). It is scanned automatically. |
| 2 · Plots | Pick your plot-boundary file (`.shp`, `.geojson`, `.gpkg`, `.kml` or a `.gdb` folder) and confirm the **PLOTID** column. Optional: treatment, block, sowing-date columns. |
| 6 · Run | Click **Run analysis**. Everything else has sensible defaults. |

Optional modules (section 5) switch on stand count, canopy cover/volume, harvestable area, plant length,
correlation, thermal stress, GDD and field-data integration. Raster GeoTIFFs are written only if you turn
that toggle on and tick layers.

## Results

In the output folder (default `outputs\` next to the app):

- `PlotStats_<date>.xlsx` – one sheet per statistic (Minimum … Range), statistics tests, correlations, thermal, GDD
- `PlotPredictors_<date>.xlsx` – one row per plot with every numeric predictor (for modelling)
- `figures\` – 350 dpi PNGs in numbered sub-folders (`01_overview` … `11_field_data`)
- `rasters\` – only when requested

## Share it

Send the zip (about 1 MB; it contains no data). The recipient follows "Install" above. Settings can be exchanged
with the **Save settings / Load** buttons in the app header.

## GPU

Optional. On a computer with an NVIDIA card, run once inside the app folder:
`.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install cupy-cuda12x` — the header badge then shows the GPU.

## Trouble?

- *"Port 8765 is already in use"* – an earlier PlotSpectra window is still open; close it.
- *Python not found* – reinstall Python with "Add to PATH" ticked, or run `PlotSpectra.bat` again after a restart.
- Anything else – the log in section 6 says what failed; `outputs\last_config.json` holds the settings used.
